chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There was nothing more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than remaining hungry and fearful for the sake of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What was the most beloved state to the Prophet Muhammad according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) preferred enduring hunger and fear of God over worldly ease, highlighting the virtue of *khawf* (awe/reverence) as a catalyst for spiritual elevation. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s asceticism (*zuhd*) not as mere deprivation, but as a conscious state of divine vigilance that deepens one’s connection to Allah.
